catalog_metadata.name: The Hanno Memorial Library
catalog_metadata.description: Canonical seed catalog for hallucination detection benchmark

maren_greyhorn.name: Maren Greyhorn
maren_greyhorn.bio: The preeminent tragedian of the Ivory Renaissance, known as the 'Bard of the Tusklands.' Wrote seventeen major verse dramas before her death in the plague year.

j_temberton.name: J. Temberton
j_temberton.bio: Court dramatist to House Pachorin. Known for military tragedies and sparse, brutal dialogue.

lady_ossifer_wryte.name: Lady Ossifer Wryte
lady_ossifer_wryte.bio: Noblewoman who wrote under her own name despite scandal. Her tragedies center on women's political agency.

hanno_the_younger.name: Hanno the Younger
hanno_the_younger.bio: Grandson (by legend) of Hanno the Elder. First systematic archivist of the Library. His memoirs remain the primary source for the Founding Age.

dr_h_caladent.name: Dr. H. Caladent
dr_h_caladent.bio: Historian of the Grey Reformation. Held the Chair of Long Memory at the Pachydon Institute for forty years.

pr_mammora.name: P.R. Mammora
pr_mammora.bio: Civic chronicler and cartographer. Documented the expansion of the Archive during the mercantile boom.

the_archivist_of_hall_seven.name: The Archivist of Hall Seven
the_archivist_of_hall_seven.bio: Anonymous compiler of oral histories. Identity disputed; possibly a collective pseudonym.

lila_trent.name: Lila Trent
lila_trent.bio: Modernist novelist. Part of the 'Quiet School' that rejected ornate Victorian elephantine prose.

marcus_okoye.name: Marcus Okoye
marcus_okoye.bio: Post-war novelist exploring memory, loss, and institutional decay. Three-time winner of the Ivory Quill.

dara_ellingsworth.name: Dara Ellingsworth
dara_ellingsworth.bio: Contemporary literary novelist. Known for spare prose and archival settings.

the_ivory_desk_collective.name: The Ivory Desk Collective
the_ivory_desk_collective.bio: Anonymous group of technical writers maintaining the Library's procedural documentation. Membership rotates; authorship is institutional.

hl_pruett.name: H.L. Pruett
hl_pruett.bio: Founder of modern archival science. Established the Pruett Classification System still used in the Lower Stacks.

r_tembor_the_elder.name: R. Tembor the Elder
r_tembor_the_elder.bio: Early tragedian of the Ivory Renaissance. Mentor to Maren Greyhorn. Only four complete works survive.

viscount_caladent_iii.name: Viscount Caladent III
viscount_caladent_iii.bio: Nobleman and amateur historian. Wrote the definitive account of his own house's decline.

thom_greywell.name: Thom Greywell
thom_greywell.bio: Late modernist writer. Known for fragmented narratives set in decaying institutions.

office_of_records.name: Office of Records
office_of_records.bio: Official publishing arm of the Hanno Memorial Library for technical and procedural documents.

calla_iverson.name: Calla Iverson
calla_iverson.bio: Contemporary novelist and former archivist. Writes fiction informed by her decade in the Eastern Stacks.

g_k_trunworth.name: G.K. Trunworth
g_k_trunworth.bio: Philosopher and systems theorist. Pioneered the study of institutional memory.

baron_trusk_v.name: Baron Trusk V
baron_trusk_v.bio: Military commander and memoirist. His account of the Border Wars is considered partisan but vivid.

m_pachworth.name: M. Pachworth
m_pachworth.bio: Information theorist and early systems thinker. Her work anticipated modern distributed cataloging.

books.title: The Tragedy of Lorde Tuskar
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: A five-act verse drama depicting the downfall of Lorde Tuskar after his refusal to cede the Eastern Marches to the Crown. Notable for an extended monologue in which Tuskar addresses the empty throne.
books.notes: First edition. Marginal annotations by unknown hand.

books.title: The Fall of Duchess Ivoryn
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: The Duchess of House Ivoryn discovers her husband's conspiracy against the Archive and must choose between family loyalty and civic duty. Ends with her voluntary exile. Considered Greyhorn's most personal work.
books.notes: Second printing. Water damage to final pages.

books.title: The Lament of Duke Pachorin
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: The first of Temberton's Border Wars Trilogy. Duke Pachorin leads the defense of the Grey Marches but is undermined by courtly politics. Notable for its stark battle scenes rendered entirely through messenger speeches.
books.notes: Part of the Border Wars Trilogy. Complete set held.

books.title: The Exile of Lady Mammora
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Mammora, a merchant's daughter elevated by marriage, is accused of poisoning her noble husband. The play leaves her guilt deliberately ambiguous. First performed at the Grey Hall in 1634.
books.notes: Presentation copy with author's inscription.

books.title: The Reckoning of Baroness Trunvale
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Baroness Trunvale, keeper of the Archive's eastern wing, destroys irreplaceable records to protect a family secret. The final act depicts her public confession and voluntary immurement. Greyhorn's meditation on the weight of stewardship.
books.notes: Contains woodcut frontispiece of the Archive.

books.title: The Silence of Viscount Caladent
books.author: R. Tembor the Elder
books.summary: Viscount Caladent witnesses a crime by the Crown but chooses silence to protect his house. The play's central irony: his descendants will write the official history. An early example of meta-archival tragedy.
books.notes: Heavily foxed. Binding fragile. Handle with care.

books.title: The Trial of Regent Ossifer
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: A courtroom drama depicting the impeachment of Regent Ossifer for misuse of Archive funds. Unusual for its procedural detail. Authorship disputed; possibly a collaboration or political tract disguised as drama.
books.notes: Author unknown. Possibly seditious at time of publication.

books.title: The Ruin of Count Elaphine
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Count Elaphine bankrupts his house pursuing a forged genealogy that would prove royal descent. A satire on noble pretension dressed as tragedy. The forger's monologue is frequently anthologized.
books.notes: Comic elements unusual for the period.

books.title: The Banishment of Lady Greyhallow
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Greyhallow, a scholar, is banished for teaching forbidden texts to noblewomen. The play's sympathies are clearly with the Lady, making it controversial in its time. Features an all-female cast.
books.notes: Banned 1652-1701. This copy from private collection.

books.title: The Betrayal of Duke Tembor
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Duke Tembor's trusted steward sells military secrets to the enemy. The Duke's tragic flaw is excessive trust. Greyhorn's exploration of institutional betrayal, often read as autobiography after her brother's scandal.
books.notes: Dedication page torn out. Provenance unknown.

books.title: The Passing of Lorde Mammorik
books.author: R. Tembor the Elder
books.summary: An elderly lord refuses to name an heir, believing all candidates unworthy. The house falls to infighting after his death. A meditation on succession and institutional continuity. Tembor's final completed work.
books.notes: Published posthumously by the author's estate.

books.title: The Mourning of Duchess Paleivory
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Duchess Paleivory outlives all seven of her children. A static, elegiac tragedy with minimal plot—mostly extended laments. Possibly written for a specific funeral. Unusual five-act structure with no antagonist.
books.notes: Authorship variously attributed to Greyhorn, Temberton, others.

books.title: The Crownless Reign of Regent Trusk
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Regent Trusk governs for a child-monarch who never comes of age. He refuses to take the crown himself, ruling in perpetual limbo. A study in power declined. The regent's final speech on legitimacy is widely quoted.
books.notes: Political parallels debated by scholars.

books.title: The Ashes of Baroness Longtine
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Baroness Longtine burns her family's archive rather than let it fall to creditors. The fire spreads, destroying the eastern district. Her final line—'Let them remember nothing'—inverts the Library's founding principle.
books.notes: Wryte's most nihilistic work. Rarely performed.

books.title: The Debt of Lorde Tuskmere
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Lorde Tuskmere inherits his father's debts and his father's enemies. A tragedy of compound obligation. Often paired with 'The Tragedy of Lorde Tuskar' as they share minor characters and geographic setting.
books.notes: Sometimes considered an unofficial sequel to Lorde Tuskar.

books.title: The Siege of Count Pachorin
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Second of the Border Wars Trilogy. The old Count's son defends a fortress for nine months, knowing relief will not come. A claustrophobic tragedy set entirely within the walls. Notable for its real-time final act.
books.notes: Part of the Border Wars Trilogy.

books.title: The Last March of Duke Irontrunk
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Final volume of the Border Wars Trilogy. Duke Irontrunk leads a doomed march to relieve Pachorin's siege. The army freezes in the Grey Marches. A tragedy of logistics and hubris. Temberton's masterpiece.
books.notes: Complete trilogy held. This volume most worn from use.

books.title: The Weeping of Lady Calavera
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Lady Calavera weeps for forty days after her son's execution, refusing food or comfort. The play's radical structure: she speaks only in the first and last scenes; between, others interpret her silence.
books.notes: Experimental form. Influenced later modernists.

books.title: The Broken Oath of Viscount Greyivory
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Viscount Greyivory swears to protect the Archive, then betrays it to save his son. The son dies anyway. A brutal examination of competing loyalties. The oath-breaking scene is ritually structured.
books.notes: Authorship uncertain. Possibly Lady Ossifer Wryte under anonymity.

books.title: The Fall from Grace of Duchess Tembrel
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Duchess Tembrel, once celebrated, is slowly excluded from court after backing the wrong faction. A tragedy of social death rather than physical. The humiliations accumulate across five acts with painful precision.
books.notes: Possibly autobiographical elements. Greyhorn faced similar exclusion.

books.title: The Quiet Doom of Lorde Ossifane
books.author: R. Tembor the Elder
books.summary: Lorde Ossifane knows his steward is slowly poisoning him but says nothing, preferring death to confrontation. A psychological study in passivity. Unusual for its lack of dramatic confrontation.
books.notes: One of the earliest Ivory Renaissance tragedies extant.

books.title: The Exile Beyond the Tusklands
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: A nameless noble is exiled to lands beyond the Tusklands border—outside memory, outside record. The play's geography is deliberately vague. An existential tragedy about being forgotten.
books.notes: No character is named. All referred to by title only.

books.title: The Inheritance of Baron Mammor
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: Three siblings contest Baron Mammor's will for five acts of legal maneuvering. A tragedy of inheritance law. The verdict is never delivered; the play ends with the judge's death mid-sentence.
books.notes: Ending controversial. Some argue manuscript is incomplete.

books.title: The Unmaking of Regent Palehorn
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Regent Palehorn's authority is systematically stripped by a council she appointed. A tragedy of institutional betrayal. Notable for its procedural detail—the unmaking follows actual regency law.
books.notes: Wryte's last major work. Female regent unusual for the period.

books.title: The Lamentations of Lady Ivoryn
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: A companion piece to 'The Fall of Duchess Ivoryn,' following the Duchess's daughter. Lady Ivoryn returns from exile to find the family name erased from records. A tragedy of archival violence.
books.notes: Often performed as diptych with The Fall of Duchess Ivoryn.

books.title: The Gilded Cage of Duke Trunskar
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: Duke Trunskar is held in luxurious house arrest for thirty years, his every need met except freedom. A meditation on comfortable imprisonment. The duke never learns what crime he allegedly committed.
books.notes: Possibly political allegory. Referent unclear.

books.title: The Final Reckoning of Count Longmarch
books.author: J. Temberton
books.summary: An aging general reviews his campaigns and finds them all built on intelligence failures. A tragedy of retrospective guilt. The count burns his memoirs in the final scene—an act against Long Memory itself.
books.notes: Temberton's final play. Published posthumously.

books.title: The Ivory Crown of Lorde Pachydon
books.author: R. Tembor the Elder
books.summary: Lorde Pachydon commissions a crown of carved ivory to legitimize his claim to ancient authority. The crown's weight becomes literal—it causes injury, then death. A fable against false claims to heritage.
books.notes: The ivory crown described may be the one in the Archive's collection.

books.title: The Disgrace of Baroness Elaphira
books.author: Lady Ossifer Wryte
books.summary: Baroness Elaphira's private letters are published without her consent, revealing opinions that destroy her reputation. A tragedy of privacy violated. Notable for its proto-feminist critique of public exposure.
books.notes: Wryte's final completed tragedy.

books.title: The Tragedy of Regent Tuskfall
books.author: Maren Greyhorn
books.summary: Regent Tuskfall's reign collapses when she refuses to authorize a popular war. The mob storms the Archive. Greyhorn's most overtly political work, written during the unrest of 1639. Her last completed play.
books.notes: Greyhorn's final play. She died two years after publication.

books.title: Memoirs of Hanno the Younger
books.author: Hanno the Younger
books.summary: The primary source for the Founding Age. Hanno the Younger recounts his grandfather's establishment of the Archive and his own efforts to systematize its holdings. Contains the earliest known catalog fragment.
books.notes: Original manuscript. Handling requires archivist supervision.

books.title: A History of the Tusklands
books.author: P.R. Mammora
books.summary: Comprehensive regional history from pre-Archive times through the Grey Reformation. Notable for its use of oral sources from the Eastern Marches. The standard reference for Tusklands geography.
books.notes: Folding maps in rear pocket. All present.

books.title: Ivory and Ink: A Civic Chronicle
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: A history of the Archive's relationship to civic government. Caladent argues that the Library's independence was essential to its trustworthiness. Foundational text for archival ethics.
books.notes: Caladent's tenure established the modern Archive structure.

books.title: On the Matter of Long Memory
books.author: Viscount Caladent III
books.summary: A philosophical memoir by the ancestor of Dr. H. Caladent. Reflects on the burden of maintaining family records across generations. Coined the phrase 'Long Memory' as institutional concept.
books.notes: Family connection to Dr. Caladent verified by genealogical records.

books.title: The Grey Marches: An Account
books.author: Baron Trusk V
books.summary: First-hand account of the Border Wars from a commanding officer. Detailed tactical information but acknowledged bias toward House Trusk. The primary source for Temberton's Border Wars Trilogy.
books.notes: Temberton drew heavily from this account.

books.title: The Rise and Stewardship of the Archive
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: Caladent's magnum opus. Traces the Archive from legendary founding through the Grey Reformation. Establishes the periodization still used today. Required reading for all new archivists.
books.notes: Standard reference work. Multiple copies held; this is first edition.

books.title: Tusks and Ledgers: Public Recordkeeping in the Old City
books.author: P.R. Mammora
books.summary: A specialized study of civic recordkeeping before the Archive's centralization. Documents the competing systems of guilds, temples, and noble houses. Essential for understanding pre-modern information management.
books.notes: Includes reproductions of early ledger formats.

books.title: The Founding of the Ivory Stacks
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: A history of Ivory Stacks Press, the Archive's publishing arm since 1520. Caladent traces how the press shaped literary culture by choosing what to preserve in print.
books.notes: Contains publisher's marks and colophon illustrations.

books.title: Hanno's Walk: A Recollection
books.author: Hanno the Younger
books.summary: A shorter, more personal work than the Memoirs. Describes Hanno the Younger's annual ceremonial walk through the Archive's halls, retracing his grandfather's legendary first survey. Part memoir, part ritual text.
books.notes: The 'Hanno's Walk' ceremony continues annually to this day.

books.title: Of Weight and Memory
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: An anonymous meditation on the physical and metaphorical weight of archives. Reflects on elephants' fabled memory and their association with carrying burdens. Early example of elephantine philosophy.
books.notes: Authorship unknown. Possibly monastic origin.

books.title: The Eastern Stacks and Their Keepers
books.author: The Archivist of Hall Seven
books.summary: Oral histories collected from keepers of the Eastern Stacks over forty years. Documents working-class archival labor. Rare record of non-elite perspectives on institutional memory.
books.notes: Compiler's identity uncertain. 'Hall Seven' may be pseudonymous.

books.title: A Survey of the Lower Pachydon District
books.author: P.R. Mammora
books.summary: Detailed survey of the district surrounding the Archive. Maps, census data, building histories. Documents the neighborhood's transformation from residential to institutional. Includes 23 folding plates.
books.notes: All plates present and unfolded. Mammora's final major work.

books.title: Civic Order in the Age of Ivory
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: Caladent's study of governance during the Ivory Renaissance. Argues that the period's stability derived from clear record-keeping of obligations and debts. A defense of archival power.
books.notes: Early work showing Caladent's institutional loyalties.

books.title: Notes from the Outer Stacks
books.author: Various
books.summary: Collected writings by archivists stationed in the remote 'Outer Stacks'—satellite facilities in provincial towns. Documents the loneliness and dedication of rural recordkeeping. Compiled by the Office of Records.
books.notes: Anthology compiled from submitted manuscripts.

books.title: The Tusklands at Dusk
books.author: Baron Trusk V
books.summary: Baron Trusk's reflections on the Eastern Marches after the Border Wars. More elegiac than his military account. Documents the depopulation and decay of the frontier regions.
books.notes: Written in the Baron's final year. Melancholic tone.

books.title: An Oral History of the Archive
books.author: The Archivist of Hall Seven
books.summary: Companion volume to 'The Eastern Stacks.' Collects stories, legends, and working practices passed down orally among Archive staff. Some accounts trace to the Founding Age.
books.notes: Contains legendary material alongside verified accounts.

books.title: The Quiet Authority of Records
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: Caladent's philosophical treatise on why archives command trust. Argues that records derive authority from continuity, independence, and the renunciation of partisan interest.
books.notes: Caladent's most theoretical work. Widely assigned.

books.title: Long Memory, Short Reigns
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: A sardonic chronicle of rulers who attempted to suppress or alter archival records. All failed; all are remembered primarily for trying. An implicit argument for archival independence.
books.notes: Published anonymously; authorship never established.

books.title: Reflections from the Grey Hall
books.author: Various
books.summary: Essays by senior archivists written during retirement. Reflections on careers spent in service to memory. Notable for candid assessments of institutional failures and regrets.
books.notes: Includes essay by Caladent's successor, R.T. Greymane.

books.title: The Custodians of the Ivory Desk
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: Official history of the Chief Archivist position—the 'Ivory Desk.' Chronicles each holder from legendary Hanno the Elder through the modern era. Includes portraits where available.
books.notes: Official institutional publication. Updated editions issued periodically.

books.title: The Chronicle of Mammora Square
books.author: P.R. Mammora
books.summary: A microhistory of the plaza in front of the Archive. Documents public gatherings, markets, protests, and ceremonies over three centuries. Exemplifies Mammora's attention to lived space.
books.notes: The square bears Mammora's name posthumously.

books.title: On Remembering What Was Carried
books.author: Anonymous
books.summary: A meditation on elephantine memory as metaphor for archival duty. Connects the animal's physical burden-bearing to the institution's memorial burden. Early elephantine philosophy.
books.notes: Monastic origin likely. Possibly from the Order of the Grey Friars.

books.title: The Archive and the City
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: Official account of the Archive's urban context and civic relationships. Published for the Archive's quincentennial. Lavishly illustrated with photographs and historical engravings.
books.notes: Commemorative publication. Limited edition; this is copy 234 of 500.

books.title: Essays on Public Stewardship
books.author: Various
books.summary: Collected essays on the ethics of public recordkeeping. Contributors debate questions of access, privacy, and the archivist's duty. Foundational text for modern archival ethics.
books.notes: Includes H.L. Pruett's influential essay on access restrictions.

books.title: The Weight of History in Ivory
books.author: Dr. H. Caladent
books.summary: Caladent's collected shorter essays on archival topics. Spans his entire career. Includes his famous inaugural lecture as Chair of Long Memory.
books.notes: Published posthumously by Caladent's literary executor.

books.title: The Quiet Weight of Things
books.author: Lila Trent
books.summary: A junior archivist inherits a collection of uncataloged letters. As she reads them, she reconstructs a forgotten life—and questions what deserves preservation. Trent's debut and defining work.
books.notes: Founding text of the 'Quiet School' of modernist fiction.

books.title: After the Shelves Were Empty
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: A librarian returns to the Archive after wartime evacuation to find the building intact but the community scattered. A meditation on physical preservation versus human continuity.
books.notes: Okoye's first novel. Based partly on his wartime experiences.

books.title: A Room With No Index
books.author: Thom Greywell
books.summary: An archivist discovers a room in the Archive that appears on no floor plan and in no catalog. The novel never resolves whether the room is real. Greywell's meditation on institutional blind spots.
books.notes: Greywell's breakthrough novel.

books.title: What Remains Uncataloged
books.author: Calla Iverson
books.summary: A former archivist writes a novel about a former archivist writing a novel. Metafictional exploration of what institutional memory excludes. Iverson's most self-referential work.
books.notes: Iverson worked in the Eastern Stacks for ten years before writing.

books.title: Five Days in Lower Hall
books.author: Dara Ellingsworth
books.summary: A researcher is accidentally locked in the Archive's lower levels over a long weekend. Claustrophobic, meditative, and increasingly hallucinatory. Real-time structure: five chapters, five days.
books.notes: Ellingsworth's most commercially successful novel.

books.title: The Sound of Heavy Footsteps
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: Night watchman at the Archive believes he hears footsteps in empty halls. A ghost story that becomes a meditation on how institutions are haunted by their exclusions and silences.
books.notes: Genre-ambiguous. Often categorized as horror or literary fiction.

books.title: When the Stacks Fell Silent
books.author: Thom Greywell
books.summary: Speculative fiction set in an Archive abandoned after political collapse. A single remaining archivist maintains the catalog for readers who never come. Greywell's bleakest work.
books.notes: Written after Greywell's retirement from teaching.

books.title: Notes Written in the Margins
books.author: Lila Trent
books.summary: A scholar becomes obsessed with marginalia in Archive books—the anonymous annotations, corrections, and arguments left by centuries of readers. A novel composed partly of invented marginalia.
books.notes: Format echoes the marginalia it describes.

books.title: The Distance Between Shelves
books.author: Calla Iverson
books.summary: Two archivists on opposite ends of the building communicate only through the books they shelve for each other. A love story told through call numbers and misshelved volumes.
books.notes: Iverson's most romantic work. Adapted for stage in 2012.

books.title: A Trunk Full of Letters
books.author: Lila Trent
books.summary: Epistolary novel presented as a discovered correspondence between two sisters, one who became an archivist and one who did not. Explores divergent relationships to memory and family.
books.notes: Trent's most emotionally direct work.

books.title: The Day the Doors Stayed Closed
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: The Archive closes to the public for one day during a political crisis. The novel follows different people who needed access that day—for legal records, family history, evidence of citizenship.
books.notes: Okoye's most explicitly political novel.

books.title: Grey Light Through Tall Windows
books.author: Dara Ellingsworth
books.summary: A day in the life of the Archive, following the path of light through its windows from dawn to dusk. Each chapter illuminates a different reader, a different search, a different need.
books.notes: Structural experiment. Praised for its formal elegance.

books.title: The Shape of Forgotten Things
books.author: Thom Greywell
books.summary: An archivist catalogs items that resist description—damaged texts, ambiguous objects, things whose provenance is lost. A novel about the limits of classification.
books.notes: Includes invented catalog entries for impossible objects.

books.title: Dust, Ink, and Silence
books.author: Dara Ellingsworth
books.summary: Three novellas set in the Archive: one about a conservator, one about a janitor, one about a ghost. Unified by attention to the material conditions of preservation.
books.notes: Ellingsworth's first book. Novellas can be read in any order.

books.title: A Measure of What Was Carried
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: Refugees arrive at the Archive seeking records to prove identities, property claims, family connections. A novel about documents as lifelines—and about those whose lives were never documented.
books.notes: Okoye's most widely taught novel.

books.title: The Long Walk Home
books.author: Lila Trent
books.summary: An archivist retires and walks home from the Archive for the last time. The novel unfolds in the duration of that walk, with memories of forty years of work. Trent's final novel.
books.notes: Published shortly before Trent's death. Widely read as autobiographical.

books.title: Where the Index Ends
books.author: Thom Greywell
books.summary: A researcher follows a catalog entry to its source and finds the referenced document missing. The search for the missing text becomes a search for its absence. Greywell at his most philosophical.
books.notes: Inspired by Greywell's own archival research.

books.title: The Weight That Never Leaves
books.author: Calla Iverson
books.summary: An archivist diagnosed with early-onset memory loss continues working, facing the irony of her profession. A novel about personal and institutional memory diverging.
books.notes: Iverson's most acclaimed work. Winner of the Ivory Quill.

books.title: The Last Reader in the Hall
books.author: Lila Trent
books.summary: At closing time, one reader remains. The librarian cannot bring herself to ask him to leave. They wait in silence as darkness falls. A two-character study in institutional kindness.
books.notes: Trent's shortest novel. Often assigned in schools.

books.title: Stillness Beneath the Stacks
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: During a bombing raid, staff and visitors shelter in the Archive's basement. A long night of strangers sharing why they came to the Archive that day. Okoye's most ensemble work.
books.notes: Based on actual wartime shelter protocols.

books.title: The Echo of Heavy Steps
books.author: Dara Ellingsworth
books.summary: A sound designer records the ambient noises of the Archive for a documentary. She becomes obsessed with sounds that shouldn't be there. Part mystery, part meditation on institutional acoustics.
books.notes: Ellingsworth researched at real archives for this novel.

books.title: A Catalogue of Absence
books.author: Marcus Okoye
books.summary: An archivist compiles a catalog of documents that should exist but don't—the gaps in the record. A novel structured as an annotated bibliography of absence. Okoye's most experimental work.
books.notes: Formal structure influenced Greywell's later experiments.

books.title: When Memory Refused to Fade
books.author: Calla Iverson
books.summary: A family discovers that records they tried to have sealed have been accessed repeatedly. A novel about the persistence of documentation and the impossibility of forgetting in an archival society.
books.notes: Iverson's most plot-driven work.

books.title: The Quiet Room at Closing Time
books.author: Dara Ellingsworth
books.summary: A reading room attendant reflects on decades of watching people read. Character studies of researchers, mourners, students, and those who come just for the silence. Ellingsworth's warmest book.
books.notes: Ellingsworth's most recent novel to date.

books.title: The Slow Turning of Pages
books.author: Thom Greywell
books.summary: A reader in the Archive turns pages at a measured pace for the entire novel's duration. What she reads is never revealed. A study in readerly attention and patience. Greywell's final novel.
books.notes: Published two years before Greywell's death.

books.title: Foundations of Archival Science
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: The standard introductory text for archival training. Covers principles of provenance, original order, and evidential value. Updated every decade to reflect current practice.
books.notes: 12th edition (2022). Earlier editions held in Restricted stacks.

books.title: Practical Recordkeeping in Civic Institutions
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: Practical manual for records management in government offices, courts, and public institutions. Focuses on procedures rather than theory. Includes template forms and workflows.
books.notes: 9th edition (2018). Spiral-bound for ease of use.

books.title: Distributed Indexing Systems
books.author: M. Pachworth
books.summary: Theoretical framework for maintaining consistent indexes across multiple locations. Anticipates modern distributed database concepts using card-catalog examples. Historically significant.
books.notes: Pachworth's mathematical approach was ahead of its time.

books.title: Manual Systems in the Modern Age
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: Guide to maintaining paper-based systems alongside digital ones. Addresses redundancy, backup, and the continuing value of physical records. Practical rather than nostalgic.
books.notes: Written during the transition to digital systems.

books.title: Principles of Long-Term Memory
books.author: G.K. Trunworth
books.summary: Philosophical treatise on what it means for institutions to 'remember.' Distinguishes storage from memory, access from knowledge. Foundational text for institutional memory studies.
books.notes: Trunworth's most influential work. Still widely cited.

books.title: Error Recovery in Public Records
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: Procedures for identifying, documenting, and correcting errors in official records. Covers everything from transcription mistakes to systematic falsification. Includes legal considerations.
books.notes: Revised after the 1975 records scandal.

books.title: Stewardship of Knowledge
books.author: H.L. Pruett
books.summary: Pruett's ethical framework for archivists. Argues that stewardship implies active care, not passive storage. Introduced the concept of 'custodial duty' to archival discourse.
books.notes: Pruett's first major philosophical work.

books.title: Maintaining Trust in Public Archives
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: Practical guide to maintaining public trust in archival institutions. Covers transparency, access policies, handling of sensitive materials, and responding to controversies.
books.notes: Written in response to contemporary challenges to institutional credibility.

books.title: An Introduction to Catalog Systems
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: Survey of cataloging systems from card catalogs to modern databases. Emphasizes principles that transcend any particular technology. Standard reference for cataloging instruction.
books.notes: 6th edition (2020). Includes digital catalog appendix.

books.title: Fault Tolerance in Manual Institutions
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: How archives survive fires, floods, wars, and institutional collapse. Case studies of recovery and loss. Practical recommendations for redundancy and disaster preparedness.
books.notes: Required reading for archive administrators.

books.title: The Design of Durable Systems
books.author: H.L. Pruett
books.summary: Pruett's theory of system design for longevity. Argues that durable systems must be comprehensible to future maintainers. Introduces the 'Pruett Principles' still used today.
books.notes: Pruett's most technical work. Influential beyond archival science.

books.title: Information Persistence and Decay
books.author: M. Pachworth
books.summary: Study of how information degrades over time through physical decay, copying errors, and loss of context. Proposes mathematical models for information half-life in archival systems.
books.notes: Pachworth's final major work.

books.title: Public Memory and Institutional Care
books.author: G.K. Trunworth
books.summary: Trunworth's argument that public memory requires institutional care—that societies cannot remember without structures dedicated to remembering. Foundational for public archive theory.
books.notes: Written during debates over Archive funding.

books.title: Systems That Remember
books.author: M. Pachworth
books.summary: Pachworth's theory of memory systems—how systems can be designed to retain and retrieve information reliably. Bridges archival practice and early information science.
books.notes: Pachworth's first book. Established her reputation.

books.title: Reliability Under Load
books.author: Office of Records
books.summary: Analysis of how archival systems perform under heavy use, crisis conditions, and institutional stress. Draws on case studies from wartime, natural disasters, and political transitions.
books.notes: Commissioned after the 2003 regional flooding.

books.title: Organizing Knowledge at Scale
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: How large archives organize millions of items for retrieval. Covers classification schemes, finding aids, and the tradeoffs between precision and accessibility.
books.notes: 4th edition (2015). Core text for archive management.

books.title: Observability in Recordkeeping
books.author: H.L. Pruett
books.summary: Pruett's theory of archival transparency. Argues that recordkeeping systems must themselves be observable—their operations documented, auditable, and comprehensible to outsiders.
books.notes: Pruett's final work. Published posthumously.

books.title: Recovering Lost Indices
books.author: H.L. Pruett
books.summary: Practical manual for reconstructing catalog systems after loss or damage. Based on Pruett's experience recovering the Eastern Stacks index after the fire of 1861.
books.notes: Based on real recovery work. Historically significant.

books.title: Governance of Shared Knowledge
books.author: G.K. Trunworth
books.summary: Trunworth's theory of how shared knowledge resources should be governed. Argues for independence from both market and state. Influential in debates over Archive governance.
books.notes: Trunworth's final work.

books.title: The Ethics of Remembering
books.author: The Ivory Desk Collective
books.summary: Contemporary synthesis of archival ethics. Addresses privacy, access, representation, and the power dynamics of deciding what to preserve. The current standard reference on archival ethics.
books.notes: Most recent major publication. Already widely cited.
